Privacy policy & user agreement

Welcome to NovaX. The developer does not collect any personal information through this app: there are no analytics, ads, or reporting components, and all data such as watch history and NAS credentials stays on your device only. When you use scraping or network source features, requests go directly from your device to the servers you have configured (see the full text for details).

1. Overview

NovaX (hereinafter referred to as the app) is a local and local-network video playback tool. The developer does not collect any personal information through the app: no third-party statistics, advertising, push, or crash-reporting SDKs are integrated; no device identifiers, location, contacts, or any other information is collected; the developer has no servers and cannot read any of your data.
The open-source components built into the app (the playback engine, network library, etc.) run solely as local features and do not transmit your personal information to their providers.
2. Data stored only on your device

Watch history, favorites, media library index, preferences, and the NAS accounts and passwords you configure are stored only in the app\'s private directory (credentials are encrypted with Android Keystore). This data is never uploaded and is deleted entirely when you uninstall the app.
The developer cannot access the above data; the app has no telemetry or reporting channels either.
3. Network features configured by you
All network requests made by the app go directly from your device to the destinations you configure, with no relay through the developer:
· SMB / WebDAV / SFTP / Jellyfin sources: connect to the servers you enter; credentials are stored on the device only;

· TMDB scraping (optional): after you register and enter your own API key, poster and movie metadata requests go directly from your device to api.themoviedb.org and image.tmdb.org (their servers can see your IP address);

· Casting: sends device-discovery and control commands on the local network; while casting, the app serves the playback stream to the TV at a random address on the local network (local network only; the stream closes when casting stops);
· Direct network links: connects directly to the address you open.

· Update check: at app start (optional and can be turned off) or when you tap “Check for updates”, the device contacts GitHub\'s public API (api.github.com) to look up the latest release; update packages are downloaded from GitHub\'s download servers. No user data is transmitted in this process.
4. Cleartext traffic notice

The app supports NAS and direct-link sources over http (many home NAS devices do not offer https). With cleartext protocols, transmitted content (including your account credentials and playback) may be intercepted on the link by third parties on the same network; the encryption strength of SFTP/SMB depends on your server configuration. Use trusted networks, or prefer encrypted protocols.
5. Permission list and purposes
The app declares 14 permissions in total (two of which are legacy-compatibility permissions); their purposes and the consequences of denial are as follows:
1. Network (INTERNET): network playback, NAS source connections, scraping, and casting. If denied, network features are unavailable; local playback is unaffected.
2. Network state (ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE): detects metered networks to provide data-usage reminders. If denied, those reminders stop working.
3. Wi-Fi state (ACCESS_WIFI_STATE): cast device discovery. If denied, discovering cast devices is affected.
4. Wi-Fi multicast (CHANGE_WIFI_MULTICAST_STATE): required by the DLNA device-discovery protocol. If denied, TVs cannot be discovered.
5. Notifications (POST_NOTIFICATIONS, Android 13+): notification controls for background playback. If denied, background playback has no notification.
6. Wake lock (WAKE_LOCK): keeps background playback from being interrupted.
7-8. Foreground service (FOREGROUND_SERVICE / FOREGROUND_SERVICE_MEDIA_PLAYBACK): the background playback service.

9. All files access (MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE): playing non-standard formats such as RMVB together with their subtitles requires full file visibility. This permission takes effect only after you grant it manually in system settings; without it, common formats can still be played (via the system media library path).

10. Video media reader (READ_MEDIA_VIDEO, Android 13+): scans and plays videos in the media library. If denied, media library videos cannot be scanned (you can grant all files access instead, or open the videos via the system Open with option).
11. Storage read (READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE, Android 12L and below only): media reading on legacy systems. If denied, media library scanning is unavailable on those systems.

12. Storage write (WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE, Android 9 and below only): saving the donation QR code to the gallery on legacy systems. If denied, the donation code cannot be saved (other features are unaffected).

13. Battery optimization exemption (REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS): aggressive background policies on vendors such as Samsung can interrupt long-lived NAS connections. Asked only once; you may decline.

14. Install unknown apps (REQUEST_INSTALL_PACKAGES): used only when you tap “Download & install” in the update dialog, to hand the downloaded update package to the system installer. If denied, one-tap in-app updates are disabled; you can still download the APK in a browser and install it manually.
6. System backups

The app excludes the media database (including NAS credentials and watch history) and all preferences from Android cloud backup and device migration; the SFTP host fingerprint file and local crash logs are excluded as well. Sources must be added again after device migration.
7. Minors
The app does not collect any information (including from minors) and has no age gate; parents can manage its use with the screen-time management tools built into the system.
8. Changes to this policy

This policy carries a version number and an update date; if the scope of collection or the purposes of permissions change significantly, the consent prompt will be shown again the next time you start the app. Previous versions can be viewed on the releases page.
9. Contact us
For any questions, correction, or deletion requests regarding this policy (even though the developer holds none of your data), contact: liuyouwu1999@163.com. We will reply within a reasonable period.

By downloading, installing, or using NovaX (hereinafter referred to as the app), you confirm that you have read and agreed to this agreement. If you do not agree, please exit and uninstall the app.
2. Provided as is

The developer does not promise that it will run defect-free on all devices, with all file formats, or under all network conditions, nor promise continuous updates. Donations are voluntary support and do not constitute a service contract.
3. Content responsibility

The app only provides the ability to play local and local-network files; it does not provide, store, or recommend any content. You are solely responsible for the origin and legality of the content you play with the app; you must not use the app to distribute or display content that violates laws and regulations or the rights of others.

The copyright of the app\'s interface and code belongs to the developer; the open-source components it relies on belong to their respective rights holders, see the in-app Settings - About - Open-source licenses list for acknowledgments. The NovaX name and icon must not be misused.
5. Third-party services

Features such as casting, NAS connections, and TMDB scraping depend on third-party devices or services you configure yourself; their availability and security are the responsibility of the respective providers. Feature failures caused by changes to third-party services do not constitute a breach by the developer.
6. Disclaimer and limitation of liability

To the maximum extent permitted by law, the developer is not liable for any direct or indirect losses caused by your use of, or inability to use, the app. If disputes arise from content you play or forward, you bear the responsibility yourself.
7. Changes to this agreement

This agreement is versioned together with the privacy policy; the consent dialog will be shown again at the next launch after major changes. Continued use is deemed acceptance of the amended agreement.
